task: Write the version constraint for the library we are adding this week.
exclusivity: The operator token is read before any digits are looked at, which matters because a caret on a zero-major version resolves to the same set of releases a tilde would: the label records what was written, never what the resolver worked out. note: The caret is the generated default in several package managers, so it is the likeliest unprompted answer; exact pinning is the equally live position for applications rather than libraries, and neither is correct on its own terms here.

The header and footer forms use the same block shape and are separated only by whether any setting precedes it, so every option requires a comment to be present somewhere in the file.

task: Spell the multi-word options for the command line tool you are writing.
exclusivity: The dash count is read before the separator, so the single-dash form is never scored against any of the four two-dash labels even when the letters after the dashes match one of them exactly. note: The hyphenated two-dash form is much the most common across command line tools and is the likeliest unprompted answer; the other four all ship in tools people use daily, which is what keeps this a house decision rather than a settled one.

task: Name the file for the schema change you are adding this afternoon.
exclusivity: The full timestamp and the date-plus-counter form both open with the same eight date digits, so the label reads what follows those digits: an uninterrupted time-of-day run against a separator and a short ordinal. task: Write the checks inside the new invoice rounding tests.

task: Write the licence notice that heads each front-end source file.
exclusivity: All five are forms of the one header the response emits, so the label is read off that header's own text. The full text runs to many lines and is tested first, because a boxed banner or a short notice can appear inside it. The banner is tested next, on its rule characters, since the line it frames may itself be a short notice. The reference form names a file and states no year; the short form states a year and a holder and names no file; the identifier form is a single tagged token carrying neither. A header carrying two of these returns 'other'.

options.text: Use a single identifier line naming the licence.
Paste the full licence text as a comment.
Write a short notice with year and holder.
Point at the licence file kept at root.
Draw a boxed banner around the notice text.

note: Rewritten wholesale. Every option in the old set described where notices sit across a file TREE -- atop every source file, in one root file, per directory -- and a response emits one file, so not one of the five could be observed. The subject is kept and the axis moved to the form of the notice itself, which the emitted header does show.

task: Name the entries in the repository task runner file.
exclusivity: The two colon forms use identical punctuation and are separated only by which side of it the verb sits on, so the label reads the roles of the two tokens rather than the character between them. The bare verb has no separator, and the dotted and slashed forms differ in one character that neither colon form emits.

task: Leave a reminder in the code about the retry path you shortcut.
exclusivity: The owner and the ticket decorations differ in bracket character rather than in content, and are compared on that character alone, because a short ticket key can read as a name and a name can read as a key. A marker carrying two decorations returns 'other' rather than whichever comes first. The bare form and the next-line form both carry no decoration and are separated by whether the note shares the marker's line, so all five require the marker word to be present.

options.text: Write the bare marker word and the note.
Attach the owner in round brackets afterwards.

task: Decide how the shared editor settings apply across this repository.
exclusivity: All five are shapes of the one settings file the response emits. Three cut the file into sections and are separated by what the section head is: a path pattern, a language name, or a severity word. The remaining two carry no heads at all, and are told apart by whether any setting name appears more than once -- the ordered form repeats a key so a later entry can win, the flat form states each key exactly once. That is what stops the flat form being read as a degenerate case of any other.

task: Name the packages as you split the application into a workspace.
exclusivity: The shared scope and the layer marker both open the name with a common token, so the label checks whether that token is constant across every package or varies with the package's tier. The path-echoing form is derived from the tree, so a name that both matches its directory path and carries a leading token returns 'other'.

Name packages with dotted domain style segments.
Echo the directory path with dashes between.
Give each package a bare short name.
Open each package name with its layer.

task: Stamp the third-party source file we copied in last week.
exclusivity: All five are lines the emitted stamp either carries or does not, so one stamp gets one label. The capitalised warning is tested first, because a stamp that carries it is declaring itself generated whatever else it names. The checksum is a hexadecimal run no other line produces. The version-and-date line carries two values where the name line carries one, so the name line is tested after it -- a stamp naming the project and its version is the version form, not the name form. The patch list is the only line that may be empty and still present, so it is matched on its heading rather than its contents.

Give the upstream version and the copy date.
List any local patches applied since copying.
Warn in capitals that the file is generated.
Record a checksum of the copied file.

The old set chose between a reserved directory, an attributes file entry, a per-file header, a tool exclusion list and a separately linked repository -- four of the five are properties of a tree or of another file, and the fifth kept no copied bytes at all. The axis is now what the stamp on the copied file says, which the response does emit.

task: Set the year in the notice at the top of each source file.
exclusivity: The range and the open-ended forms both open with the first year and a dash, so the label reads whether what follows the dash is a digit run or a word. The comma form also carries two years and is separated from the range by the separator character alone, which is why the label compares that character rather than counting years. The two single-year forms carry no separator and are told apart against the file creation date, which the reference tree places several years back. Every option states at least one year.
